title: Fix: dedicated autoscaler burst utilization reporting edge-case and priority smoothing
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers and internal canaries observed sporadic spike in 'dedicated_burst_utilization' during short load bursts when priority routing and token-bucket smoothing were enabled. Root cause: an off-by-one/rounding case in the tokenbucket refill normalization combined with reporting that used instantaneous counters rather than a short sliding window, which caused reported utilization to exceed configured burst capacity in rare boundary cases. Summary: this PR fixes the normalization bug, moves reporting to a 5s sliding window for burst utilization metrics, clamps reported burst to the configured capacity, and ensures the smoothing factor for priority routing is applied prior to normalization. Changes include code fixes, unit tests, integration perf test adjustments, a docs note, and a small Helm values tweak for dedicated deploys. Checklist: - Fix tokenbucket normalization math and clamp reported values - Replace instantaneous counter with 5s sliding window for metrics - Add unit tests for zero-capacity and boundary refill cases - Add integration perf-canary job to reproduce and assert expected reporting behavior - Add docs/observability note and release note entry Motivation: inaccurate utilization reporting led to noisy alerting and misinformed autoscaler decisions (temporary wrong shrink/grow). This is a correctness + reliability fix; no API changes. Testing: added unit tests (autoscaler/reporting/metrics_test.go), extended perf-canary integration with a synthetic burst scenario, ran full CI (lint, unit, integration perf, e2e). The first CI run revealed a flaky perf-canary timing assertion; adjusted test timing and re-ran. Rollout/merge: safe to roll to dedicated fleets immediately; change is local to autoscaler and metrics layer. Release notes: included. See linked linear ENG-4821 for follow-ups (dashboard attribution and long-term 1m aggregations).
